global_statements.CROSS_MODEL_LATENCY_RANKING: AVAILABLE only among models whose generation ran in direct mode; NOT_AVAILABLE for a run that mixes direct and batch models
global_statements.CONFIGURED_LIMITS_SOURCE: run manifest resolved_config: stages.correctness_tests.run_timeout_seconds and stages.enhanced_tests.run_timeout_seconds; the build limit comes from stages.correctness_tests.build_timeout_seconds when configured, else the 120 s code default. An effective --run-timeout CLI override is NOT persisted by the producer and must be declared to the validator
global_statements.PROVIDER_COST_RULE: LLM usage tokens x configured price only; generation and repair responses counted once each; missing usage stays null
global_statements.ABSOLUTE_CROSS_PILOT_RUNTIME_COMPARISON: NOT_COMPARABLE unless host/container/compiler/grid/niter identities match the pinned runtime condition of both runs

fields.producer: thesis/generation/common.py:apply_direct_timing (generation main loop; repair: thesis/repair/orchestrator.py direct request loop)
fields.meaning: end-to-end request latency of ONE model call as seen by the client
fields.clock_source: time.perf_counter (monotonic) when status.timing_clock == 'perf_counter'; time.time (wall clock) for legacy records (pilot_001, timing_clock absent)
fields.end_boundary: after the success/failure record fields are applied, before the record is written
fields.on_timeout: client timeout (generation_defaults.timeout_seconds) raises inside the retry loop; the final failure record still carries the observed elapsed
notes: the RETRY BACKOFF inside call_with_retries is inside the timer, and it uses generation_defaults.sleep_seconds_between_requests as its wait when that value is > 0 (otherwise an exponential backoff capped at 10 s); only the sleep AFTER the record is written is outside the timer. A retried request therefore carries its own backoff time
upper bound = timeout x (retry_attempts+1) x (sdk max_retries+1) plus the in-timer backoffs
model speed ranking only among DIRECT-mode models; a run that mixes direct and batch models has CROSS_MODEL_LATENCY_RANKING = NOT_AVAILABLE

fields.meaning: ALWAYS null: batch APIs expose no per-request inference time
consumers: build_overview (must treat null as not available)
notes: a batch record with a non-null duration_seconds is a contract violation

fields.meaning: JOB-level provider queue span shared by every request of the job
fields.clock_source: two UTC wall-clock stamps (utc_now_iso) on the client side
fields.end_boundary: the poll that observed the job completed
allowed_aggregation: per job only; never per request; never as a latency distribution
fields.on_timeout: n/a (jobs expire provider-side; expired requests are re-submitted as new jobs)
notes: NOT model latency: dominated by provider queueing (pilot_001: 6108-23884 s per job)
pilot_001 records predate this derived field; the two stamps exist

fields.meaning: provider-reported usage; reasoning_tokens is the EFFORT measure (separate from any time field)
notes: provider cost = tokens x configured price per model; generation and repair responses are counted once each (never both a base record and its repair history); missing usage stays null and is never estimated

fields.meaning: wall time of the compiler process for one sample
fields.end_boundary: after the process exits or is killed
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed stored + compile.timed_out=true (limit 120 s code default)
notes: build time, kept strictly separate from run time

fields.meaning: wall time of ONE timed benchmark process at one grid point (serial: 1; omp: OMP_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,4,8}; mpi: -np in {1,2,4,8})
fields.start_boundary: before Popen of the benchmark (or mpirun)
fields.end_boundary: after the process exits or is killed
allowed_aggregation: median per (model, benchmark, execution_model, grid point)
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed stored + runs[].timed_out=true. The limit is the manifest's stages.correctness_tests.run_timeout_seconds, BUT run_correctness.py accepts a --run-timeout override that is persisted nowhere; a run that used one must declare it (the validator takes it via --run-timeout-seconds), otherwise its legitimate timeout rows look inconsistent with the frozen limit
notes: mpi: includes_launcher_overhead=true (mpirun -np N is the timed argv) and MPI_Init/teardown; omp: includes OpenMP runtime init and the omp driver's fixed timing iterations; serial: includes process startup
RUN_SECONDS_CROSS_EXECUTION_MODEL_COMPARABLE = false

cross-model comparison within one execution model requires: same host/container, same compiler, same grid point, same niter, sequential execution (correctness stage is sequential) and no wall-clock anomaly on the row

fields.meaning: wall time of one grouped enhanced build
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed is stored, but a build that hit the 120 s limit is recorded as build_status='build_failed' - INDISTINGUISHABLE from a compile error, so an enhanced build timeout is NOT detectable from the record alone (pre-existing producer behaviour, stated here rather than assumed away)
notes: pilot_001 carries ONE wall-clock artifact: claude_opus_5 compile_seconds 70714.574 s (a host suspension mid-compile); the validator flags rows whose elapsed exceeds limit + 2 s without a timeout flag

fields.producer: thesis/evaluation/run_enhanced_tests.py (per-spec run inside the worker thread)
fields.meaning: wall time of ONE enhanced spec execution (run only, build separate)
fields.start_boundary: inside the worker immediately before Popen
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed + status='timeout' (exit_code null); limit = manifest stages.enhanced_tests.run_timeout_seconds
notes: thread pool over SAMPLES (pilot: serial jobs=2): local queue wait is outside the timer, CPU contention is inside; therefore not a speed measure
verdict-only specs legitimately carry no duration

fields.meaning: wall time of the analysis tool invocation(s) for one sample; the SCOPE differs per tool (see notes), so the includes map below is the union and must not be read per tool
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed + analysis_state=TIMEOUT (v3) / error string (legacy pilot_001)
notes: STATIC_DURATION_IS_MODEL_SPEED = false: this is analysis cost, never a property of the model

per-tool scope: parcoach records ONLY the parcoach step on success and ONLY the emit-llvm step on compile failure (includes.build is false there); cppcheck and clang_tidy perform no build of their own (includes.build false); compiler and gcc_analyzer ARE the build; infer builds under its capture. The includes map is therefore the union over the tools, not a per-tool statement

per-tool timeouts (e.g. gcc_analyzer 300 s, parcoach 60 s) live in the manifest's stages.static_analysis.tools[<tool>] settings; the validator does not yet compare them, so a timeout row's elapsed is checked for finiteness and sign only
not-applicable entries carry 0.0 with ran=false

fields.meaning: wall time of one dynamic tool's BUILD plus the SUM over its launch grid for one sample - a composite, not a single process
fields.end_boundary: after the last grid launch exits or is killed
fields.on_timeout: observed elapsed of the timed-out step + the tool's error/state; the per-tool limit lives in the manifest's stages.dynamic_analysis.tools[<tool>] settings
notes: DYNAMIC_DURATION_IS_MODEL_SPEED = false; the number aggregates build and every launch-grid point, so it is not comparable with the single-process static field
not-applicable entries carry 0.0 with ran=false

fields.meaning: assembly records carry created_at_utc only; assembly is not timed

generation_timing_classes.DIRECT_LATENCY_AVAILABLE: every generation record of the model is direct with a numeric duration
generation_timing_classes.BATCH_QUEUE_ONLY: every generation record of the model is batch (duration null, job stamps only)
generation_timing_classes.MIXED_DIRECT_AND_BATCH: the model's records mix both modes (latency distribution incomplete)
generation_timing_classes.TIMING_PROVENANCE_INSUFFICIENT: timing_mode missing/unknown or durations missing on direct records
generation_timing_classes.TEST_RUNTIME_AVAILABLE: correctness build and run timings present for the model
